create.name: Sri Ramakrishna Math Chennai
create.bio:
Sri Ramakrishna Math in Mylapore, Chennai, was the Ramakrishna Order's first centre in southern India. After Swami Vivekananda's visit to the city on his return from the West in 1897, he sent his brother monk Swami Ramakrishnananda to begin the work there; he arrived that March, and the Math moved from the Ice House, now Vivekanandar Illam, to its present site in Mylapore at the end of 1907. Today its centrepiece is the Universal Temple, whose design deliberately blends Hindu, Buddhist, Jain and European church architecture around a marble image of Sri Ramakrishna, with shrines to Sri Sarada Devi and Vivekananda on either side.

Visitors of any faith may sit in the temple for worship or silent meditation. Each evening brings arati followed by bhajans, and monks give discourses in Tamil from Tuesday to Saturday and in English on Sundays. There is an annual three-day retreat in July or August and a monthly half-day of japa for initiated devotees. The Math publishes books in Tamil and English and two monthlies, the English Vedanta Kesari, issued since 1914, and the Tamil Sri Ramakrishna Vijayam, and runs schools and charitable services. Its YouTube channel streams the evening arati daily and posts talks, Gita classes and festival worship.

courses.title: Vivekananda Sanskrit Course
courses.description: A one-year spoken Sanskrit course run with Samskrita Bharati at the Math in Mylapore, three evenings a week, aimed at reading scripture and chanting hymns with understanding; books, an examination and a certificate are included.

courses.title: The Vedanta Kesari subscription
courses.description: A print or digital (PDF and ePUB) subscription to the Ramakrishna Order's English monthly on Vedanta, spirituality and culture, published from the Math since 1914, with an enlarged themed issue each December.

free_resources.title: Evening discourses, arati and bhajans
free_resources.description: Free evening programme at the Universal Temple: arati at 6.30 pm followed by bhajans, and talks by the monks in Tamil from Tuesday to Saturday and in English on Sundays.
